high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Ise-katagami stencil illustration: one dyer inspects two cloth lengths before an open cedar archive chest; the flawless repeated cloth enters the chest, while a second cloth containing tiny off-pattern perforations remains wholly outside against a precise stencil screen, rendered as flat washi, indigo and persimmon-brown forms.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A full persimmon-brown washi field carries a restrained repeating wave-and-leaf komon around the outer margin, with a broad cream central workspace and one flat indigo ground strip. No photographic lighting, gradient, realistic room, window, landscape, perspective recession, text, calligraphy, numeral, caption, arrow, flowchart, interface, warning sign, shrine, sacred emblem, official seal, throne or national flag appears.

elements.desc: Adult Ise-katagami dyer kneeling at center, light-medium skin tone, straight black hair tied beneath a plain indigo cloth, cream work jacket, persimmon-brown apron and dark trousers. With a careful neutral gaze, they hold the irregular cloth fully outside the storage chest and align it against the stencil screen; no authority badge, weapon, crown or judging staff appears.

Tall freestanding Ise-katagami inspection screen at the left, made from three laminated sheets of persimmon-tannin washi cut with hundreds of precise cream pinholes forming one continuous wave-and-leaf komon. The screen is a working stencil rather than wall decoration and contains no writing, sacred figure, signature, caption, warning icon, numerical grid, interface control or certification seal.

Full indigo cloth length held directly against the inspection screen, carrying the expected cream wave-and-leaf repetition plus a compact cluster of irregular crimson micro-perforations between two motifs near its center. The entire cloth remains outside the chest and uncut; it has no words, letters, numerals, rejection cross, danger symbol, label, signature or transparent digital overlay.

Open low cedar archive chest occupying the lower-right, built from plain brown boards with a raised lid and one clean interior compartment. A separate flawless indigo cloth is folded halfway inside, making storage visibly later than inspection; the chest has no lock emblem, written inventory, label, ranking shelf, official crest, glowing status lamp or hidden second chamber.

Flawless indigo cloth folded into the cedar chest, carrying the same cream wave-and-leaf komon in an uninterrupted repeat with no stray holes, missing units or crimson fragments. Only this separate clean result crosses the chest rim; it has no text, number, signature, stamp, medal, ownership mark, face, religious motif or explanatory diagram.

Small carving mat at the lower-left holding one crescent knife, circular punch and fan-shaped punch beside a few clean washi cuttings. These ordinary Ise-katagami tools explain the precision of the screen without touching either cloth during inspection; the mat contains no modern scanner, computer, magnifier display, caption, numbered legend, arrow, badge or authority symbol.
